thread:
olivia: heads-up: nightly SDLC pipeline failed during verification. DAST didn't start and SAST halted because artifact unseal failed: KMS returned PermissionDenied on decrypt step (`kms-unseal-artifact`). Anyone oncall? :confused:
ben: paste logs?
nagios-bot: build excerpt:
```
ERROR: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = caller does not have permission to use resource 
resource: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ci-keys/cryptoKeys/ci-deploy-key
```
priya: that resource is explicitly bound to `group:ci-kms-ops@redwood` in IAM. I can check audit logs for SetIamPolicy.
ben: full disclosure: I ran a bulk RBAC cleanup yesterday to collapse legacy groups into the `ci-ops` umbrella. Looks like `ci-kms-ops` was one of the groups removed by the refactor. I didn't expect it to still be referenced by the KMS binding. My bad.
olivia: ok. short-term mitigation: we need to restore decrypt permission for the CI runner so SAST/DAST can finish. Prefer granting `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` to the specific service account `ci-runner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` scoped to `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ci-keys/cryptoKeys/ci-deploy-key`. No wildcard grants.
leo: applying scoped grant now and will post change-id. Also will add an annotation in the commit message referencing SEC-5420.
snyk-bot: SAST queued note: prior run flagged an RSA private key blob pattern in `ops/scripts/deploy.sh` history (low-confidence). Will re-run after artifact verifies.
priya: two parallel asks: 1) capture the SetIamPolicy audit entry and the failed Decrypt event and attach to SEC-5420 for RCA, 2) decide if the flagged RSA key in repo history is a leak or a FP; if it's a leak, rotate the key immediately and treat as incident.
ben: confirmed SetIamPolicy at 2026-06-10T23:18:02Z removed `ci-kms-ops@redwood` (actor: ben@redwood). I reverted the cleanup change that removed that group binding from the KMS key.
olivia: can we avoid this recurring? Suggestions: - require a pre-merge verification for any PR touching iam/*, infra/cleanup scripts, or the RBAC refactor tool that runs `gcloud kms keys testIamPermissions ci-deploy-key --keyring=ci-keys --location=global --permissions=cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` and fails otherwise. - add a whitelist in the cleanup script: never remove groups listed in infra/config/iam-protected.json. - add an automated policy check that flags PRs which remove an existing key-level binding.
leo: agree. I'll open PRs: 1) scoped grant revert + service-account binding, 2) ci/verify-kms-access.sh pre-merge check, 3) update cleanup to consult iam-protected.json.
priya: on the RSA key flag: I ran `git log --all --grep="BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY"` and found a historical blob committed in 2019 by a dev sandbox branch that was deleted later. It appears the key in history is likely a test key and rotated out long ago. Still, we should rotate any keys potentially used and add a forensic note. I'll mark as low-severity but recommend rotation of any keys that could be active.
ben: doing a conservative rotate of the CI key pair now, and will update the key rotation metadata. Posting the rotation change-id to SEC-5420.
sec-eng-bot: Reminder: link follow-ups to SEC-5420 and run security checklist item "CI KMS binding verified".
olivia: also improve pipeline UX: decrypt wrapper should include job name, key path, and SetIamPolicy diff link when it fails so oncall can triage faster. Right now the error hides which job and which key.
leo: will patch the decrypt wrapper to surface job_name and the key resource and return the gcloud logging link on failure.
snyk-bot: SAST result: the RSA pattern is in history only; current tree has no private key file. Marking as historical hit. Creating suppression entry with note: "historical test key; rotated and removed" once rotation confirmed.
olivia: timeline: RBAC reverted & scoped SA binding applied at 23:34Z, pipeline retried and SAST/D AST completed by 23:45Z. Actions left: (A) add pre-merge kms test (PR by leo), (B) add cleanup whitelist and safe-delete checks (PR by ben), (C) improve decrypt logging (PR by leo), (D) rotate any potentially impacted keys and add rotation metadata to SEC-5420 (priya/ben). I'll leave SEC-5420 open for the follow-ups. Thanks folks :+1:
